absent: Behaviour and failure modes of the shared vacant-span search routine and the meaning of descending, request and alignment flags.
Locking, concurrency and lifetime rules for the resource tree beyond the interrupt guard and release publication visible here.
Validation of size, alignment and descriptor arguments and handling of zero or overflowing ranges.
Full direct-memory access policy enforced by strict checks and the revocation reader that pairs with the inode publication.
Wire format and versioning of restartable-sequence user structures and critical-section descriptors.
Scheduling, migration and signal interactions that set the pending event and notify-resume flag.
Slice-extension semantics and timing parameters beyond the debug file presence.
Tracing event payloads and stability guarantees.
Complete signal forcing and fatal-delivery semantics including handler states and permission checks.

findings.text: Device-bound helper that locates a vacant span inside a supplied container for a requested length, tags it for device private use, searches from high addresses downward and claims it under the device name with default alignment.

Non-device helper with the same high-to-low claiming policy for device private use and default alignment, differing in that it carries no device association and labels the span with a caller supplied name.

Generic vacant-span allocator that accepts caller alignment, leaves the descriptor unset, and follows the default low-to-high insertion policy rather than the descending claiming policy of the private-memory helpers.
Boot-time string option that relaxes or tightens direct memory checks depending on which keyword appears, always reporting successful handling.
Pseudo filesystem descriptor for direct memory bookkeeping, identified by a short name, bound to module lifetime, using a context initializer and an anonymous-super teardown.

During early initialization the direct-memory filesystem is pinned, an anonymous inode is obtained from its superblock, failures are logged and unwound, and on success the inode reference is published with release ordering for a paired acquire reader elsewhere.
Low fixture spans value 0x0000 through value 0xffff; narrower fixtures span 0x1234 to 0x2345, 0x4567 to 0x5678, 0x6789 to 0x789a, and 0x2000 to 0x7000, each backing a static test span.
Test helper record holding two input span pointers together with an expected span value and an expected boolean outcome.

Union succeeds for containing or overlapping inputs and yields the outer bounds, while disjoint inputs fail; intersection succeeds only on overlap and yields the shared bounds; both operations are verified in either operand order with cleared output and equality checks on outcome and bounds.

Compound layout fixtures chain one-megabyte pieces in order: RAM, hole, window, RAM, then a triple-wide window, with an overlapping RAM and a smaller code carve-out inside the wide window plus trailing RAM; total extent reaches the end of the wide window.

Region-classification test that reserves a large parent span, nests RAM, window and code children inside with automatic cleanup, then checks that queries return intersecting, disjoint or mixed as appropriate for aligned, straddling, hole and boundary cases.
Test catalogue for the resource subsystem registering union, intersection and region-classification cases, terminated by an empty entry and wrapped in a named suite.
Restartable-sequence debugging is governed by a global branch flag switched through a small helper, a boot parameter accepting boolean text, and a privileged file supporting readback and user writes.

Per-CPU counters for exits, signals, slow and fast paths, identifiers, critical sections, clears and fixups, plus five slice-extension counters when that option is enabled, are summed across all possible CPUs with racy accessors and rendered as labeled decimal lines through a single-open sequence file.
Early debug filesystem setup creates a top directory and a writable control file, then attaches statistics and slice-extension entries according to build configuration.
Statistics and slice-extension initializers each have an active variant that publishes a file and an inert variant that does nothing, selected by configuration.
Two translation-unit markers request slow-path construction and trace-point instantiation for this file.

Slow-path user update skips exiting tasks, records a slow-path event, atomically snapshots and clears the scheduling flag while preserving version and interrupt state and capturing processor and memory-context identifiers, derives the node, and either refreshes user state or clears error state and raises a fault signal.
Critical-section probe that treats a zero user address as success and otherwise delegates to the update routine, reporting failure when user memory cannot be read.

Resume path that ignores a missing register frame for hypervisor guest entry and otherwise runs the slow-path user update; signal path that counts delivery, aborts any active critical section with fault escalation on failure, and forces identifier refresh for legacy mode.
Trace shims that forward task update and instruction-fixup notifications to the tracing layer.

Signal helpers that synthesize a kernel-origin descriptor for a given number and force delivery; the segmentation variant escalates to fatal handling when already fatal, while the fatal variant pins default disposition on the current task.

Faults while reading or writing restartable-sequence control fields from user memory, or encountering an out-of-range critical address during debug return, result in a forced fault signal; identifier reset writes zeroed values with an uninitialized marker and likewise faults on error. Syscall return path only validates when registration state is present.

Scheduling-event snapshot and identifier capture execute under an interrupt-masked guard to remain local-atomic against preemption, and the direct-memory inode pointer is published with release ordering to pair with an acquire load in revocation.
